title: Signed tensor comparison and composition on cochain sheaf pullbacks
statement:
Let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi on small sites: $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$, $u^{-1}$ preserves finite limits, and $u^{-1}R\to S$ is a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $u^*P=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}P$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] termwise on cochain complexes, and direct-sum total tensor with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ for $x\in P^p$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For arbitrary, possibly unbounded cochain complexes $P,Q$, the ordinary module tensor comparison induces an isomorphism of complexes
$$c_{u;P,Q}:u^*\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(u^*P\otimes_Su^*Q).$$
On local pure tensors in degrees $(p,q)$ it is $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; its inverse is $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. The maps are natural in both complex arguments. They respect the usual reassociation of triple total tensors, the signed symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$, and the two action unitors for the ring complex $R[0]$ and its pullback identification $u^*R[0]\cong S[0]$.

For any composable morphism of ringed topoi $v:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),T)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$, let $a_P:(u\circ v)^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*u^*P$ be the canonical composition comparison, obtained from the inverse-image adjunctions and the scalar multiplication $T\otimes_{v^{-1}S}v^{-1}(S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}P)\cong T\otimes_{(u\circ v)^{-1}R}(u\circ v)^{-1}P$. Then
$$(a_P\otimes a_Q)c_{u\circ v;P,Q}=c_{v;u^*P,u^*Q}\,v^*(c_{u;P,Q})\,a_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}.$$
Let $R\to R'$ and $S\to S'$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings and $\phi':u^{-1}R'\to S'$ a ring map with $u^{-1}R\to u^{-1}R'\to S'$ equal to $u^{-1}R\to S\to S'$, and let $u'$ be $u$ with coefficient map $\phi'$. For an $R$-complex $K$ put $K'=K\otimes_RR'$ termwise, and similarly over $S$. Let $\varepsilon_{P,Q}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)'\to\operatorname{Tot}(P'\otimes_{R'}Q')$, $(x\otimes y)\otimes r\mapsto(x\otimes r)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, its analogue $\varepsilon^S$ over $S$, $\kappa_K:u'^*(K')\to(u^*K)'$, $s'\otimes(x\otimes r)\mapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes s'\phi'(r)$, and $\tau_K:u^*K\to u'^*(K')$, $s\otimes x\mapsto\bar s\otimes(x\otimes1)$, be the canonical scalar-association and transition chain maps. Then
$$(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)\,c_{u';P',Q'}\,u'^*(\varepsilon_{P,Q})=\varepsilon^S_{u^*P,u^*Q}\,(c_{u;P,Q}\otimes_SS')\,\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)},\qquad(\tau_P\otimes\tau_Q)\,c_{u;P,Q}=c_{u';P',Q'}\,u'^*(\varepsilon_{P,Q})\,\tau_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}.$$
These equations hold as equations of chain maps; in particular, for quotient towers $P_m$, $Q_m$ over $R_m$, $S_m$ whose transitions are the maps $K\to K\otimes_{R_m}R_n$ ($m\ge n$), the comparisons $c_{u_m}$ commute with all transitions.

proof.text: For each pair of degrees p,q, take the S-linear module comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] for P^p and Q^q. Following its source (Stacks 03EL, the chain Hom_S(u^*(M tensor N),H) = Hom_R(M tensor N,u_*H) = Bilin(M x N,u_*H) = Bilin(u^{-1}M x u^{-1}N,H) = Hom_S(u^*M tensor u^*N,H)), it corresponds to the identity of u^*M tensor u^*N, i.e. to the u^{-1}R-bilinear map (x,y) |-> (1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y); by the module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] and the bilinear universal property of the sheaf tensor [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] its S-linear extension is s tensor (x tensor y) |-> s((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) = (s tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y), the displayed insertion of 1. Likewise the contraction (s tensor x) tensor (t tensor y) |-> st tensor (x tensor y) is well defined: it is S-bilinear and balanced over u^{-1}R in each factor, so it is induced by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and the balancing relations of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Since u^* is a left adjoint [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], it preserves the (possibly infinite) direct sum over p+q=n in the total complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; the direct sum of the degreewise maps is the degree-n map c_{u;P,Q}.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback and its proof (the chain of Hom identifications); Tag 07A4 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-tensor-product), the displayed total-complex isomorphism with these constituents

proof.text: The degree-n map is a chain map. On a homogeneous tensor x in P^p and y in Q^q, the source differential is dx tensor y plus (-1)^p x tensor dy. Naturality of the module comparison gives the same two terms after applying c, while the target total differential has exactly the same Koszul sign (-1)^p. Direct-sum inclusions then prove equality in every degree, with no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 07A4, total-complex differential and tensor comparison

proof.text: The contraction formula followed by insertion of 1 and insertion followed by contraction are identities on every local pure tensor, so c is an isomorphism with the stated inverse. The same pure-tensor calculation after applying maps P to P' and Q to Q' proves naturality in both complex arguments; equality of sheaf morphisms follows from the sheaf tensor universal property and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For three complexes, compare the two reassociation composites on a homogeneous triple tensor: both send s tensor ((x tensor y) tensor z) to (s tensor x) tensor ((1 tensor y) tensor (1 tensor z)) after the canonical associators. For the symmetry square, both routes send a bidegree-(p,q) tensor to the swapped tensor multiplied by (-1)^{pq}; for the left and right unit squares, both routes multiply by the same scalar. These are the associativity, symmetry and unit maps of the symmetric monoidal sheaf-module structure [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the total-complex signs are those of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Pure-tensor equality implies equality of the sheaf maps.

source.place: Tag 03EK, tensor associativity and symmetry; Tag 07A4, compatibility of the total-complex comparison

proof.text: For composable v and u, evaluate both sides of the displayed composition equation on a homogeneous pure tensor. The comparison a_P is obtained from the composite inverse-image adjunction; the composite-adjunction formula and the conjugate-adjunction uniqueness equation are [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Under the scalar-association identification, each route inserts the two units in the same order and then sends t tensor (x tensor y) to (t tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y). Associativity of scalar multiplication and the associator of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] make the routes equal, and naturality extends the equality to all complexes.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, canonical pullback composition; Tag 03EL, scalar-association comparison

proof.text: Coefficient square. Each of epsilon, epsilon^S, kappa, tau is induced on generators by the bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and is a chain map because it is applied termwise and commutes with the differentials d tensor 1 and 1 tensor d with the same sign (-1)^p, the scalar factor having degree 0 [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Evaluate on a local generator s' tensor ((x tensor y) tensor 1) with x in P^p, y in Q^q (such elements generate, since r is moved across by balancing [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]). Left route: u'^*(epsilon) gives s' tensor ((x tensor 1) tensor (y tensor 1)); c_{u'} gives (s' tensor (x tensor 1)) tensor (1 tensor (y tensor 1)); kappa tensor kappa gives ((1 tensor x) tensor s') tensor ((1 tensor y) tensor 1). Right route: kappa gives (1 tensor (x tensor y)) tensor s'; c_u tensor S' gives ((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) tensor s'; epsilon^S gives ((1 tensor x) tensor s') tensor ((1 tensor y) tensor 1). They agree. Transition equation: on s tensor (x tensor y), the left side gives (bar s tensor (x tensor 1)) tensor (1 tensor (y tensor 1)); the right side gives bar s tensor ((x tensor y) tensor 1), then bar s tensor ((x tensor 1) tensor (y tensor 1)), then the same element. For a quotient tower the transition K_m -> K_m tensor_{R_m} R_n is tau for R_m -> R_n, S_m -> S_n, so c_{u_m} and c_{u_n} commute with it; equality of sheaf maps follows from equality on generators.

source.place: Tag 03EL, change-of-rings compatibility of the pullback tensor comparison

proof.text: All arguments are degreewise and use only direct sums indexed by p+q=n, which u^* preserves as a left adjoint (step 1), so they apply to arbitrary, possibly unbounded cochain complexes. The chain-map, inverse, naturality, coherence, composition, coefficient-square and transition equations therefore hold as equations of chain maps; by the transition equation of step 6 they are compatible with all transitions of quotient towers.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-5b9fce69b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its parent and sibling citers, every cited statement, the unit sk-def-purity-conv and the chapter, and Stacks 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback, including its proof) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product). The statement is true. I checked by hand on pure tensors: the insertion/contraction inverses, the chain-map sign (-1)^p, the Koszul symmetry, the unitors, and both sides of the composition equation. Edge cases checked: zero complexes, the zero ring, the identity morphism, one-term complexes, negative degrees, and unbounded complexes (u^* is a left adjoint, so it preserves the infinite sums). Hypotheses and coefficient category: general ringed topoi with a ring map u^{-1}R->S. No coefficient identification and no other base-change morphism occurs. Duplicates: none found in the DAG. lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison, lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit, lem-sfb-general-sheaf-pullback-monoidal-comparisons and the derived tensor-pullback nodes differ in setting or level. There are no new nodes. Three repairs are in fixes/: (1) C3/C4: step 1 attributed the insertion-of-1 formula to lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor, whose statement gives no formula. The step now derives the formula from the 03EL Hom/Bilin chain, citing lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal and the module adjunction, and says explicitly that the infinite direct sums are preserved. (2) Route: lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction (sk-thm-properbasechange) was cited but not declared. I added tool_uses for it and for lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal. I accept those two and the declared module-pullback-tensor and sheaf-modules-tensor-closed. (3) E5: the coefficient square and the 'strict quotient towers' clause were left vague, and step 6 relied on 'transitions preserve +,*,1'. The statement now names the maps epsilon, kappa and tau and displays the square and transition equations. This makes the clause precise without weakening it, and it matches lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence. Step 6 checks both routes on generators, including the balancing checks that use the commutative-square hypothesis. Steps 6 and 7 rewritten; proof_deps recomputed. Details are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
